reason: The file-level summary is highly aligned with the implementation: it correctly captures that this file provides the TinyExpr++ runtime, built-in function library, tokenization, recursive-descent parsing, AST evaluation, constant folding, compile/evaluate entry points, comment stripping, optional leading '=', spreadsheet-style variadics, NaN-as-missing behavior, configurable operator meanings, and parser/runtime diagnostics. The function-level descriptions are also very strong and usually precise enough to reproduce the implemented behavior, including many subtle edge cases in financial functions, bitwise operations, parsing precedence, closure handling, and compile/evaluate error flows. The main gaps are a handful of implementation quirks and a few omitted built-ins/functions that exist in the file but were not described, plus one misleading detail around a bug/defaulting behavior in FV. Overall, this is close to reconstruction-ready, but not perfectly complete for a 67-hole whole-file regeneration task.
missing_functionality: Several non-hollow built-ins present in the file are not described at all, such as te_false_value, te_true_value, te_nan_value, te_max_integer, te_is_nan, te_is_even, te_is_odd, te_equal/not_equal/comparison/logical helpers, te_not, te_nominal, te_effect, te_pi, te_e, te_absolute_value, te_log/log10/pow/trig functions, te_divide, te_modulus, te_add/sub/mul, te_left_shift_or_right, te_right_shift_or_left, te_sqr, te_if, te_supports_32bit, te_supports_64bit, te_cot, te_sign, te_negate, and te_comma

The description omits the exact top-level function registry contents in m_functions, including aliases like fact/combin/permut/power/na/nan/iserr/iserror/isna and the presence of variadic flags on certain built-ins

next_token() behavior around exact operator spellings like '**', '==', '=', '!=', '<>', '<=', '>=', '&&', '||', and conditional handling of unsupported rotate/shift tokens under build flags is mostly covered, but not exhaustively enough to reconstruct every token branch verbatim

power() does not mention that multiple unary '-' operators are folded by sign toggling while multiple '~' operators collapse to a single bitwise-not effect because the implementation tracks a boolean rather than parity/count
te_compile() error position handling includes backing the recorded position up by one character when possible, which is a useful implementation detail but only briefly implied

compile() does not just strip comments conceptually; it mutates m_expression in-place while scanning for '/', including distinct handling for unterminated block comments and end-of-buffer single-line comments
incorrect_or_misleading_points: The te_fv description says non-finite presentValue defaults to 0, but the implementation actually checks !std::isfinite(presentValue) only after already requiring finite rate, nper, and pmt; more importantly, it mistakenly tests presentValue in that fallback block rather than futureValue, so the stated defaulting behavior does not match the real code

The te_right_rotate64 and te_left_rotate64 descriptions mention preserving the 63-bit limit and exact error strings, but the implementation's message is specifically 'Rotation operation must be between 0-63' with no trailing period; saying 'exact error strings' is a bit stronger than the prompt can really support elsewhere too

The file-level text says error propagation happens through either thrown runtime_error exceptions or parser error positions, which is broadly true, but evaluation() also converts runtime exceptions into parser state without throwing; the phrasing slightly understates this stateful error-conversion path

te_free_parameters() says it frees every parameter node for normal functions, but in the implementation's range-for branch it nulls only the local loop variable copy, not the stored vector elements; freeing behavior is correct, but the 'set-to-null' implication is only truly honored in the closure branch
